failure_mode: Acquisition-device variability not controlled for in validation
evidence: Chierchia et al., 2025's limitations name motion blur and inconsistent lighting as real, unaddressed sources of error in consumer-grade video capture, distinct from anything a downstream reconstruction or segmentation model can correct.
mitigation_note: named as an open limitation; blur robustness is quantified on the synthetic tier only, and a deblurring method is named as planned future work

failure_mode: Reference-object placement has no patient-guidance mechanism
evidence: Borst et al., 2025 notes that ArUco-marker placement for scale calibration depends entirely on correct unguided patient positioning, with no mechanism to guide or verify it before capture. Only one partial-occlusion case was tested, so the practical frequency is unquantified.

failure_mode: Near-universal reliance on a small set of ImageNet-pretrained backbones
evidence: The non-FM cohort (49 of this step's 56 papers) concentrates on a handful of standard architectures (ResNet variants, EfficientNet, DenseNet, VGG, MobileNet, ViT, Swin), frequently fused into dual-encoder designs, instead of wound-specific representation learning. None reports a model card or comparably structured training-data provenance statement, so whether ImageNet-derived priors capture wound-specific texture, boundary irregularity, and tissue-colour variation goes untested at both paper and field level.

failure_mode: Severe class-imbalance collapse on a minority wound type
evidence: Ni et al., 2025's best model (GoogLeNet, 88.2% overall accuracy on sharp-injury forensic classification) collapsed to 30.0% on its smallest class (slash wounds, 124 of 1,161 collected images), falling below junior forensic pathologists on that class while matching or beating senior pathologists on the two larger classes.
mitigation_note: no class-balancing, reweighting, or targeted augmentation reported

failure_mode: Possible train/test leakage via post-augmentation splitting
evidence: Wang et al., 2024 augmented 146 original DFU images to 3,000 before describing its train/validation/test split, with no explicit statement that splitting occurred at the original-image level first. If augmented variants of one source image landed on both sides, the reported 98.67% accuracy would be inflated by near-duplicate leakage instead of true generalization.
mitigation_note: not identified or addressed by the source, and not raised in its stated limitations

failure_mode: Negative transfer from insufficiently learned self-supervised pretraining
evidence: Park et al., 2024's conclusion states that downstream DFU-classification performance ``largely depends on how effectively the BYOL model learns features from unlabeled data,'' and flags degradation where that pretraining is insufficient. The caveat is stated and not demonstrated: BYOL beat the supervised-only baseline at every data proportion the paper reports.
mitigation_note: the mechanism is named without a tested fix, and without an empirical instance

failure_mode: ``Architecturally elaborate, empirically thin'' reporting
evidence: Three independent papers report no inference-time, FPS, parameter-count, or energy benchmark despite extensive architectural elaboration and explicit efficiency framing: Rifat et al., 2025 (a four-component hybrid, tagged Model Selection), and Bansal et al., 2026 and Barua et al., 2026 (both tagged Deployment). Bansal et al., 2026 carries ``lightweight'' and ``real-time'' in its own title and reports efficiency only qualitatively. The pattern recurs regardless of whether a paper self-identifies as deployment-focused.

failure_mode: Near-saturated accuracy claims warrant independent replication
evidence: Kiprono et al., 2025 reported 99.90% ensemble accuracy, including a literal 100.00% on one constituent backbone. The result is plausible given the task's class separability and has not been independently replicated by any other paper in this corpus.

failure_mode: Internal validation accuracy does not predict external generalization
evidence: Asare et al., 2025's segmentation model reached Dice 0.89 on its own held-out split and dropped to 0.62 on zero-shot external transfer to AZH (0.785 on a second external set, Medetec). The source frames this positively, as evidence of robust zero-shot transferability, and makes deployment-readiness claims alongside a call for multi-centre validation.
mitigation_note: multi-centre validation named as needed, not carried out

failure_mode: MedSAM underperforms generic SAM, replicated across two wound types
evidence: Wang et al., 2026 found MedSAM inferior to vanilla SAM on pediatric burn images (Dice 0.80 vs 0.90 with box prompts; 0.72 vs 0.86 with a single box). Taipe et al., 2024 found the same direction on DFU segmentation, MedSAM the worst of five SAM variants (IoU 0.568 against 0.941 for the best engineered zero-shot prompt). The comparators differ, so the two gaps are not on a directly comparable scale, and broad medical-domain fine-tuning measurably degrades performance on two independent wound etiologies.
mitigation_note: both papers' workaround is to prefer generic prompted SAM, not to fix MedSAM

failure_mode: Well-engineered prompting can beat fine-tuning outright
evidence: Taipe et al., 2024's combined zero-shot SAM prompt (YOLOv5-derived boxes plus superpixel-derived points) reached IoU 0.941 / Dice 0.969, beating a fine-tuned SAM baseline (IoU 0.873 / Dice 0.928) on the same DFU test set. The authors describe prompt engineering verbatim as ``a viable alternative to SAM's fine-tuning.'' This is a clean counter-example to reading the adaptation-intensity spectrum as a maturity ladder.
mitigation_note: itself a working, lower-cost alternative, demonstrated on one dataset and etiology

failure_mode: FM-based approaches degrade less under distribution shift than purpose-built CNN baselines
evidence: Hamrani et al., 2025 and Zhao et al., 2026 each report smaller cross-centre drops for vision-language-model-based systems than for conventional baselines on the same external data. In Zhao et al., 2026, a Faster R-CNN detector's mAP@0.5 fell from 48.35% to 20.54% under external validation while its GLIP-based ensemble system fell from 68.50% to 57.85% (single-model GLIP: 61.55% to 50.01%). The claim is about relative performance only: Baseman et al., 2025 fits the same pattern, outperforming all five of its non-FM baselines under naturalistic diverse-skin-tone deployment, and still reached only 54.4% Dice. Degrading less than a CNN does not guarantee degrading to an acceptable absolute level.
mitigation_note: , and only in that relative sense

failure_mode: Multimodal fusion does not reliably outperform single-modality input
evidence: Mousa et al., 2025 fused RGB wound images (ViT branch) with body-location data (transformer branch) for wound-type classification on 730 AZH images, framing location fusion as a clear improvement. Its own results complicate that: on the 4-class task the best image-only configuration reached 0.8123 accuracy while image-plus-location fusion variants spanned 0.8007 to 0.8342 depending on which metaheuristic tuned the network's hyperparameters, so three of four fusion configurations underperformed the best image-only result. Location data helped only under a specific, untransferable optimizer choice.
mitigation_note: no configuration-selection method is proposed that would reliably capture the best-case result

failure_mode: Hallucination in FM-generated clinical descriptions, traced to training-data inheritance
evidence: Busaranuvong et al., 2025's stated primary drawback is that Wound-BLIP ``occasionally generates incorrect descriptions,'' traced to inherited inaccuracy in the GPT-4o-generated captions used as its own fine-tuning data. Separately, Choudhary et al., 2025 documented a zero-shot medical VLM (Lingshu-7B) confabulating unsupported specifics, including time elapsed since surgery, which is not visible in any image, in 2 of its 7 qualitative examples, with only one of the seven correctly naming both incision and infection.
mitigation_note: both name the mechanism without testing a fix

failure_mode: A specific tissue-colour hallucination example
evidence: Chang et al., 2025's own qualitative example table shows a generated description reading ``partially red'' where the clinical reference reads ``partially pink'' for the same Stage 4 pressure-injury image; the generated text also drops ``necrotic.'' This is a clinically meaningful visual-attribute error present in the paper's own reported example and not flagged as an error by its authors.

failure_mode: Stage 3/4 pressure-injury boundary confusion, replicated across three papers
evidence: Chang et al., 2025 reports Stage 3 as its weakest F1 (73.17%, lowest of six grades); Lott et al., 2026's per-stage deferral analysis gives Stage 3 the highest deferral rate (68.3%); and Fard et al., 2025's confusion matrix shows Stage III/IV as the dominant residual off-diagonal band (21 of roughly 37 errors), even though its prose claims improved III/IV discrimination. The difficulty is specific to this clinical boundary and not to pressure-injury staging generally.
mitigation_note: Lott et al., 2026's selective-prediction mechanism lets the system abstain more often on Stage 3, managing the error without resolving the underlying confusion

failure_mode: Quantified inter-rater label noise, with a mechanism linking it to model performance
evidence: Fard et al., 2025 reports a wound-care clinician with over 35 years of experience disagreeing with the PIID dataset's own ground-truth pressure-injury stage in 36 of 84 reviewed images (43%). Basiri et al., 2024 reports Cohen's of 0.05--0.15 (``slight agreement'') between its own two clinician raters, over five DFU images. Basiri et al., 2025 supplies the mechanism connecting both: WIfI subcategories with below 0.4 consistently showed reduced accuracy across every model evaluated, fine-tuned or zero-shot. Ground truth quality gates model performance as much as model choice does.
mitigation_note: no consensus-labelling or noise-robust training method is tested against it

failure_mode: Automated metrics and LLM-judged quality disagree on which system is best
evidence: Durgapraveen et al., 2025 found an automated metric (deltaBLEU) and LLM-as-judge clinical-quality scoring disagreeing on which of two compared systems performed better, a direct caution against treating any single automated metric as sufficient evidence of output quality at this step.
mitigation_note: the disagreement is reported and left unresolved, with no combined or preferred metric recommended

failure_mode: A benchmark's own reported dataset size is internally inconsistent
evidence: Xu et al., 2025 states 697 images in its abstract, 686 in its Methods and Table 1, and a train/test/validation split of 480/173/69 that sums to 722; a separately stated 7:1:2 ratio reconciles with none of the three. This is a documented internal-consistency issue in the corpus's own evidence base, worth flagging for anyone citing this benchmark's exact scale instead of its headline findings.
mitigation_note: not identified or corrected by the source

failure_mode: Fairness collapse under naturalistic, diverse-skin-tone deployment
evidence: Baseman et al., 2025's Mask R-CNN baseline dropped from 90.2% Dice on the AZH Wound Care dataset to 39.5% on a naturalistic dataset collected at a safety-net DFU clinic; four further baselines fell from 72.9--90.3% to 18.3--36.0%. The authors' own adapted pipeline improved on every baseline and still reached only 54.4% Dice. The paper attributes the gap to naturalistic capture conditions, skin tone, and the small pixel share its wounds occupy, acting together. This remains the corpus's only FM-track Validation paper built on a purpose-collected, demographically targeted dataset with an adapted pipeline.
mitigation_note: in the fairness sense: the paper re-trains extensively, which is its proposed contribution, but performs no skin-tone-stratified analysis and tests no tone-specific mitigation, listing subgroup fairness analysis as future work

failure_mode: External and cross-dataset validation is rare across the corpus, and not only for fairness
evidence: Only 5 of Validation's 18 tagged papers run any cross-dataset or external evaluation. The pattern recurs at nearly every step where the question has been checked: 1 of 8 in Deployment, 0 of 5 in Acquisition. Preprocessing/QC is the one exception at 2 of 4, a rate this survey attributes to that step's small sample size and does not treat as evidence against the field-level pattern. The field mostly validates models on data resembling their own training distribution, of which the fairness collapse in Entry 20 is one instance among several.
mitigation_note: a field-level reporting gap with no norm, guideline, or incentive change proposed in the corpus

failure_mode: Race-based subgroup validation is not skin-tone validation, and the two are conflated
evidence: Muaddi et al., 2025's authors explicitly acknowledge that their bias analysis used patient-reported race instead of a Fitzpatrick or other skin-tone scale; in the paper's published discussant exchange the presenting author agrees that ``race does not equal skin color at all'' and states that Fitzpatrick stratification is in progress. Baseman et al., 2025 likewise never measures skin tone on a validated scale and never reports its own cohort's racial composition, despite a naturalistic diverse-deployment framing.
mitigation_note: Muaddi et al., 2025's authors state a move to skin-tone stratification is underway; it has not been executed or published

failure_mode: Discrimination metrics alone do not establish clinical rule-in/rule-out validity
evidence: Muaddi et al., 2025 reached an SSI-detection AUC of 0.81 while its recall was only 0.53, missing roughly half of actual surgical-site infections despite the favourable headline metric. The paper's published discussant exchange presses directly on this: one discussant asks whether the design target should be accuracy at all or ruling out infection, and the authors concede the model needs further refinement.
mitigation_note: debated in the discussant exchange, not resolved with a revised threshold or operating point

failure_mode: Accuracy and inter-run reliability are independent, non-substitutable dimensions for general-purpose MLLMs
evidence: Guler et al., 2026's repeated-inference design (5 runs 4 models 50 burn images) found the two dissociated on burn depth: the most reliable model reached Fleiss' =0.916 without the highest accuracy, while the most accurate model was not the most reliable. The dissociation is task-specific and does not recur on the paper's total-body-surface-area task, which is a further caution against reading either dimension as a stable model property. Single-query evaluation, the norm throughout the rest of this corpus, cannot detect it, since it never repeats a query on one input.
mitigation_note: the repeated-inference design detects the dissociation without resolving which property to prioritize for deployment

failure_mode: Visual recognition capability does not transfer to clinical decision-making, even within one model on one image
evidence: Guler et al., 2026 found burn-depth classification exceeding a majority-class baseline in every one of four tested MLLMs (50.0--62.7% against 41.7%), while surgical-indication and treatment-recommendation accuracy fell below their baselines in every model. Surgical errors were overwhelmingly false negatives (52.6--75.8% sensitivity) in a cohort where 95% of cases required surgery, with negative predictive value never exceeding 14.8%. Full end-to-end pathway correctness reached 2.7--29.3%, so the perception-to-decision gap compounds along the clinical pathway instead of attenuating.
mitigation_note: the gap is decomposed stage-by-stage; no intervention is tested

failure_mode: Tension between FM compute footprint and the field's stated low-compute deployment preference
evidence: Model Selection's FM evidence trends toward larger, heavier checkpoints, while Deployment's clearest design target, stated explicitly across Bansal et al., 2026, Borst et al., 2025, and Borst et al., 2024, is the opposite: small, fast, patient-facing, edge-runnable. The step's one FM-track entry, Barua et al., 2026, restates the tension as a design goal (``optimized for edge execution'') without naming or benchmarking a model that would satisfy it.

failure_mode: Offline benchmark metrics and real-world deployment behaviour rank models differently
evidence: Borst et al., 2024 compared seven model variants and found the lightweight architectures close together on held-out IoU and DSC, with U-Net leading, then judged the TopFormer family visually superior at distinguishing real wounds from wound-coloured decoy objects in a live six-scene phone test that no held-out metric captured. Downstream in the same group's pipeline, Borst et al., 2025 selected VWFormer with a ConvNeXt-S backbone for production despite its placing fifth of twelve on out-of-distribution mIoU (77.2 against TransNeXt-Tiny's 79.4), because clinicians chose its masks as best far more often than any competitor (35.0% against 8.3% expert choice rate).
mitigation_note: the group's workaround is to weight live-scene testing and clinician preference over offline benchmark rank; the live test covered six scenes, and the expert-choice comparison one reader study

failure_mode: Digital-divide and over-reliance risk, named by the authors themselves
evidence: Borst et al., 2025's authors identify over-reliance on the app, including patients forgoing necessary in-person consultation and clinicians becoming less vigilant in verifying AI output, and unequal digital-device access and literacy, as real risks of patient-facing AI-assisted wound care, distinct from and additional to the system's technical accuracy. These are raised in the paper's practical and societal impact discussion and were not measured in its usability studies.

failure_mode: Acquisition-stage class imbalance propagates directly into downstream segmentation quality
evidence: Chairat et al., 2023's calibration-and-correction pipeline improved cross-condition comparability overall, but downstream segmentation was tissue-type dependent: necrotic-tissue IoU (0.155) lagged far behind granulation-tissue IoU (0.642), which the authors trace to severe under-representation of necrotic tissue in their own collected dataset and not to a calibration failure. This is a collection-time imbalance problem that no downstream calibration or segmentation-model choice can correct.
mitigation_note: the cause is identified without a tested fix

failure_mode: Capture-success rate is device-platform dependent, a failure mode only a live clinical pilot surfaced
evidence: Vasconcelos et al., 2024's real-time capture-guidance system succeeded in automatic mode 44% of the time on Android against 85% on iOS, with most automatic-mode failures occurring at the focus-verification stage instead of at wound localization or adequacy checking, and mean acquisition time more than twice as long on Android. This device-dependent reliability gap surfaced only through a prospective, real-device clinical pilot; no held-out benchmark evaluation would have revealed it.

failure_mode: A vision-capable model can decline to answer at a rate that accuracy computed over answered cases conceals entirely
evidence: Apichonbancha et al., 2026 scored three frontier multimodal models on 450 wound photographs and recorded Gemini Advanced returning no usable output in 67--68% of images across several assessment domains, including 88.2% non-response on BWAT-framework scoring. A model answering one image in three is not comparable to one answering all of them, yet the two produce accuracy figures on the same scale, and no paper in this corpus reports non-response alongside accuracy as a matter of course. Takahashi et al., 2026 is the counter-example that shows the alternative is available: it reports parsed predictions for all 1,091 images under every model and prompt condition.
mitigation_note: the rate is measured and reported, with no reporting convention or metric adjustment proposed
